Post Hearing Reply Brief of                                                         2
Burnet County Commissioners Court
 TO THE HONORABLE ADMINISTRATIVE LAW JUDGES:

        Burnet County Commissioners Court (“BCCC”) submits this Post-Hearing Reply

Brief in the Joint Application of Oncor Electric Delivery Company LLC. (“Oncor”) and LCRA

Transmission Service Corporation (“LCRA”) to Amend Their Certificates of Convenience and

Necessity for the Bell County East Switch to Big Hill Substation 765-Kv Transmission Line

Project In Bell, Burnet, Concho, Coryell, Lampasas, Llano, Mason, McCulloch, Menard, Milam,

Mills, San Saba, Schleicher, Tom Green, and Williamson Counties (“Joint Application”).

   I.        SUMMARY OF ARGUMENT

        BCCC’s arguments relating to adequacy of routes and notice are set forth in its

Initial Brief and will not be addressed again.

        The Joint Applicants did not provide an updated environmental assessment based

upon the sworn testimony and evidence in the record. The burden now falls on the ALJ’s

and Commission to decipher the accurate information. The sworn testimony and record

evidence provided by intervenors should be given the same weight of credibility as the

sworn testimony and evidence provided by Joint Applicants.

        Joint Applicants failed to address in any way Burnet County’s issues relating to

interference from the transmission towers and lines with BCCC’s emergency management

communication systems and its connection to the Statewide Interoperability Communication

System.

          Finally, Joint Applicants did not carry their burden to show need for these massive

745kV transmission lines at this time.




Post Hearing Reply Brief of                   3
Burnet County Commissioners Court
     II.       CONSTRAINTS

          As discussed in its Initial Brief, BCCC’s three witnesses, all elected officials of Burnet

County, testified to their concerns regarding the potential of the transmission towers and

lines to interfere with their emergency public safety communications systems.1

          Burnet County erected several communication towers across the northern portion of

the county to ensure communication with emergency providers is not interrupted.2 On cross

examination of the Joint Applicants’ panel of witnesses, it was clear that none had experience

or knowledge as to how transmission lines can interfere with emergency public safety

communication infrastructure nor did they know where the BCCC towers were located.3 The

main witness testifying on the issue, Mr. Dave Elliot, testified that he reviewed an EPRI article

the Saturday night before the hearing.4 Mr. Elliott could only answer questions relating to

interference between the general frequency of the transmission lines to what he assumed

frequency was for the emergency communications infrastructure. Mr. Elliott admitted that

independent of the operating voltage interference, interference with radio communications

could occur driven by “gap discharge” and “corona discharge.”5 Mr. Elliott testified that the

Joint Applicants were testing for that.6 Finally, Mr. Elliott did not know what Fresnel Zone

Encroachment was, nor how it could interfere with emergency public safety communication




      1 BCCC Exhibit 1 at BCCC000021:21-BCCC000022:8; BCCC Exhibit 2 at BCCC000047:16-

BCCC000048:2; and BCCC Exhibit 8 at BCCC000072:16-BCCC000073:9.
          2 Id. at BCCC000019-BCCC000020.

          3 Tr. Vol. 2 at pp. 26:25-28:25.

          4 Id. at pp. 31:19-32:5.

          5 Id.

          6 Id. at p. 30:13-18.




Post Hearing Reply Brief of                       4
Burnet County Commissioners Court
 infrastructure. 7 Finally, Mr. Elliot admitted that Joint Applicants have not done any studies

regarding these issues.8

        Obviously, because Joint Applicants did not know what Fresnel Zone Encroachment

was, they have no idea whether the placement of the transmission lines or towers will

interfere with the emergency public safety communication towers installed in Burnet County.

Neither the ALJs nor the Commission should allow Joint Applicants to use BCCC’s emergency

public safety communication infrastructure as a test case. Literally, lives are at stake.

        Thankfully, Ms. Cooley speaking on behalf on Oncor, stated that both applicants would

work with Burnet County Commissioners Court to mitigate any issues may arise.9 Taking

that sworn testimony as true, Joint Applicants should have no problem with adding ordering

paragraphs that achieve this purpose. Further, as it is obvious from the record that Joint

Applicants do not fully understand the issues, BCCC requests that the final order include an

ordering paragraph requiring Joint Applicants to study and test issues, including Fresnel

Zone Encroachment, gap discharge and corona discharge before the lines are built.

    PUC Staff witness, John Poole, agreed that preventing interference with BCCC’s

emergency public safety communication systems was sufficiently important for the

Commission to include in the order.10

        Suggested Ordering Paragraphs are as follows:

        1. Before completing engineering and design of any transmission towers or lines,

            Joint Applicants shall commission a study on the potential interference of 765kV

            transmission lines and towers with Burnet County Commissioners Court’s



        7 Id. at p. 32:6-14.

        8 Id. at p. 31:7-18.

        9 Id. at pp. 33:22-34.6.

        10 Id. at 147;18-23.




Post Hearing Reply Brief of                    5
Burnet County Commissioners Court
                  emergency public safety communications systems, including potential Fresnel

                 Zone Encroachment, gap discharge interference and corona discharge

                 interference.

           2. Joint Applicants shall survey the location of Burnet County emergency

                 communication towers in Burnet County to determine the actual locations of the

                 emergency public safety communication towers.

           3. Joint Applicants shall consult with Burnet County Commissioners Court to

                 mitigate any potential interference with Burnet County’s emergency public safety

                 communications systems.

    III.         NEED

           Many intervenors argue that Joint Applicants have not carried their burden for the

Commission to approve the Joint Application.11 The Burnet County Commissioners Court

agrees with those intervenors. BCCC also supports the other elected Legislative officials

who filed the Amici Curiae in this docket requesting that the element of need in all of the

CCNs be delayed until this docket is completed. 12 The Legislators believed that the

Permian Basin Reliabilty Study's underlying assumptions were being actively examined

on a more complete record in this docket.13 With the lack of time for discovery on Joint

Applicants’ rebuttal, and only thirteen minutes for each intervenor to cross examine Joint

Burnet County Commissioners Court
 Applicants’ panel, BCCC does not believe that the record is sufficiently complete to

examine this issue. BCCC believes more time should be used to consider these specific

issues and make the right decision for Texas.

        As Save the Lampasas notes, the evidence reflects that the entire project’s need

is not urgent.14 Joint Applicants’ rely solely on ERCOT studies from two years ago

trying to predict a 12-year timeline for relieving load needs, without providing any

analysis of the need for additional transmission for this specific project. 15 And, as

stated in BCCC’s Initial Brief, the predicted load information has changed.16 These

changes warrant further study. Commission precedent favors careful review and

more time to ensure routes meet statutory and environmental standards.17

        As the Amici Curiae brief points out, the Texas Legislature expressly authorized

the Competitive Renewable Energy Zone transmission buildout. 18 But the PBRP was

approved by the Commission without similar legislative authorization.19

        Joint Applicants and other utilities argue that because of the current market design,

transmission is the only method over which the Commission has authority to address the

lack of capacity in the Permian Basin. 20 ERCOT and the Joint Applicants offered a

Burnet, and Lampasas Counties, Texas, Docket No . 37448, Order at 1 (Apr 28, 2010).

of Motion to Defer Determination of Need a p. 5 (Item 6327).



Post Hearing Reply Brief of                         7
Burnet County Commissioners Court
 transmission-only solution. Transmission-only solutions do not solve the problem of

sufficient dispatchable generation capacity.

         The market design has evolved since 2001; several changes were made in an

attempt to address the issue of dispatchable generation. The changes thus far have not

encouraged new dispatchable generation in ERCOT in the locations that it is needed.

Would further incentives entice such new dispatchable generation? Would the cost of the

incentives be less than the transmission-only option. There are other measures that can be

taken outside of complete market design, but perhaps a complete market design is what is

necessary. A legislative session begins in January and can address these issues. At that

time all of the citizens of Texas, through their elected officials, should be allowed a seat at

the table to discuss alternatives. This is necessary to ensure that the transmission lines

approved by the Commission are indeed necessary and the only way to address the

problem. Such deliberate measure can avoid unnecessary and irrevocable harm to Texas

lands.

         BCCC agrees with the arguments made by American Stewards of Liberty (“ALS”)

in its request to delay the determination of need, 21 but requests that before any

determination of need is made, that the Commission order ERCOT, the utilities and all

other interested stakeholders to update the Permian Basin study and consider additional

alternative methods to meet the need.

   IV.        CONCLUSION

         BCCC respectfully requests that the ALJs and the Commission reject the Joint

Application because:


         21




Post Hearing Reply Brief of                    8
Burnet County Commissioners Court
        a. the information in the environmental assessment in inaccurate and stale;

       b. the study area was unnecessarily narrow and did not make appropriate use of

           compatible right of way;

       c. legislation did not order that the solutions to the Permian Basin need be limited

           to transmission-only; and

       d. the information in the ERCOT PBRS is limited to transmission-only.

       In the alternative, BCCC requests that the decision in this docket be delayed until

the additional deficiencies as stated above are corrected.

       If the ALJs and Commission find that the Joint Applicants carried their burden in

this proceeding, BCCC requests that ordering paragraphs be included as follows:

       1. Before completing engineering and design of any transmission towers or lines,

           Joint Applicants shall commission a study on the potential interference of 765kV

           transmission lines and towers with Burnet County Commissioners Court’s

           emergency public safety communications systems, including potential Fresnel

           Zone Encroachment, gap discharge interference and corona discharge

           interference.

       2. Joint Applicants shall survey the location of Burnet County emergency

           communication towers in Burnet County to determine the actual locations of the

           emergency public safety communication towers.

       3. Joint Applicants shall consult with Burnet County Commissioners Court to

           mitigate any potential interference with Burnet County’s emergency public safety

           communications systems.
